info.title: Katika Digital Escrow Platform
info.description:
The **Katika Digital Escrow Platform** provides a secure way to manage peer-to-peer transactions in the Cameroonian market. 
 It holds funds in escrow until delivery is confirmed, offering built-in dispute resolution and Mobile Money payouts.

 ### 🔐 Security & Authentication
 *   **OAuth2 (Client Credentials):** Used for machine-to-machine communication.
 *   **JWT (RS256):** All requests must include a valid Bearer token.
 *   **MFA (TOTP):** Enhanced security for user accounts via 6-digit verification codes.
 *   **HMAC-SHA256:** Webhooks and verification codes are secured via timing-safe HMAC validation.

 ### 🚀 Key Business Flows
 1.  **Escrow Lock:** Funds are frozen in the buyer's wallet upon payment confirmation via webhook.
 2.  **QR Release:** Sellers are paid when the buyer scans a unique QR verification code.
 3.  **Payouts:** Funds can be withdrawn to Mobile Money (Campay/Monetbil) after OTP verification.
 4.  **Dispute Management:** Integrated arbitration system for handling failed deliveries or disagreements.

 ### 🛠️ Developer Resources
 *   **Base Currency:** All amounts are in **XAF (FCFA)**.
 *   **Environments:** Use the `Sandbox` server for testing integration without real funds.
 *   **Idempotency:** Webhooks use a dual-layer deduplication strategy (Redis + PostgreSQL).
 *   **Error Handling:** Standard HTTP status codes are used. 422 is returned for business rule violations.

 ---
 *Powered by [Bytesmind Engineering](https://bytesmind.tech)*

get.description: Returns a paginated list of the authenticated user's payout requests.

post.description: Creates a payout request and sends a 6-digit OTP to the user for verification. Rate-limited.

403.description: Cannot create payouts for other users

post.description: Debits the wallet and submits the payout to the Mobile Money provider. Requires prior OTP validation.

422.description: OTP not validated or insufficient funds

post.description: Validates the 6-digit OTP code. Rate-limited to 3 attempts per 5 minutes.
Deactivates MFA on the account. Requires a valid TOTP code or backup code for verification.
Verifies the first TOTP code to activate MFA. Step 2 of enrollment — confirms the user has scanned the QR code.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of transactions where the authenticated user is buyer or seller. Filter by one or more statuses (comma-separated).

post.description: Creates a new escrow transaction in INITIATED status. The authenticated user is the seller; the buyer is identified by their registered phone number. Platform fee is 3% of grossAmount (rounded down). Use idempotencyKey to safely retry on network failures — the same key always returns the same transaction.

400.description: Validation error (invalid phone, amount out of range, non-integer amount)

404.description: No Katika account found for the buyer phone number

409.description: Seller and buyer cannot be the same user

post.summary: Generate or regenerate a QR verification code
post.description: Seller-only. Generates a new HMAC-SHA256 verification code for the buyer to finalize the transaction. Allowed from LOCKED, SHIPPED, or DELIVERED status. Any previously issued QR code is immediately invalidated.

403.description: Only the seller may generate the QR code

422.description: Transaction is not in LOCKED, SHIPPED, or DELIVERED status

post.description: Seller confirms shipment. Transitions the transaction from LOCKED to SHIPPED, allowing the buyer to scan the QR code upon delivery.

403.description: Only the seller may call this endpoint

422.description: Transaction is not in LOCKED status

post.description: Validates the QR verification code and releases frozen funds from buyer to seller. Transitions the transaction to RELEASED.

422.description: Invalid verification code or wrong transaction state

post.description: Buyer confirms that the item has been received. Transitions the transaction from SHIPPED to DELIVERED. Only the buyer of this transaction may call this endpoint.

403.description: Only the buyer may call this endpoint

422.description: Transaction is not in SHIPPED status

post.description: Cancel a transaction before it is shipped. INITIATED → CANCELLED (no wallet action). LOCKED → REFUNDED (frozen funds returned to buyer). Both buyer and seller may cancel.

403.description: Only a transaction participant may cancel

422.description: Transaction cannot be cancelled in its current state

post.description: Buyer submits the scanned QR code to finalize the transaction. Validates the HMAC-SHA256 code, transitions SHIPPED→DELIVERED if needed, then releases the escrow funds (DELIVERED→RELEASED) atomically.

403.description: Only the buyer of this transaction may scan the QR code

404.description: Transaction not found or QR code expired

422.description: Invalid, exhausted, or already used verification code

get.description: Returns a paginated list of disputes where the authenticated user is initiator or respondent.

post.description: Opens a dispute on an escrow transaction. Transitions the transaction to DISPUTED and posts a system notification in the dispute room.

403.description: Cannot open disputes for other users

422.description: Transaction state does not allow disputes

post.description: Resolves a dispute with one of 5 resolution types (FULL_REFUND_BUYER, RELEASE_TO_SELLER, PARTIAL_REFUND_BUYER, SPLIT_50_50, NO_ACTION). Restricted to SUPPORT, ADMIN, and SUPERVISOR roles.

403.description: Only support staff can resolve disputes

post.description: Uploads a file as evidence for a dispute. Supports images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP), PDF, and plain text. Max 10 MB. File type is validated by magic bytes, not client Content-Type.

201.description: Evidence uploaded and broadcast to dispute room

400.description: Invalid file type or size exceeds 10 MB

post.description: Pay the court submission fee for a dispute in AWAITING_ARBITRATION_PAYMENT. Once both parties have paid, the dispute is automatically referred to the court.

200.description: Fee recorded. If both parties have now paid, dispute is referred to court.

409.description: Already paid, deadline passed, or wrong status

200.description: List of applications owned by the authenticated user

post.description:
Creates a developer application and generates the **first API key** (returned once in `initialApiKey.secret`).

**For clients with their own authentication system:** use the `API_KEY` strategy (default).
Your backend includes the key as `X-Api-Key: ktk_live_...` on every request to Katika.
Your users authenticate in your own system; Katika sees your application identity.

**Rate limits by tier:**
| Tier         | Per Hour | Per Day   |
|--------------|----------|-----------|
| FREE         | 100      | 1 000     |
| BASIC        | 500      | 10 000    |
| PROFESSIONAL | 2 000    | 100 000   |
| ENTERPRISE   | 10 000   | unlimited |

Contact support to upgrade your tier.

201.description: Application created — contains the initial API key secret (shown once)

400.description: Validation error or terms not accepted

post.description:
Generates a new webhook signing secret for your application.
Use this secret to verify that incoming webhook events originate from Katika by checking the
`X-Katika-Signature` header: `HMAC-SHA256(secret, request_body)`.
The secret is shown **once** — store it securely.

get.summary: List API keys for an application
get.description: Returns all keys (active and inactive). The `secret` field is never returned here.

post.description: Generates a new API key for the application. The `secret` field in the response is shown **once** — store it securely.

201.description: API key created — contains the secret (shown once)

400.description: Maximum number of active keys reached (10 per application)

post.description:
Immediately revokes the existing key and generates a replacement with the same label and environment.
The new `secret` is shown **once** in the response — the old key stops working immediately.

201.description: New key created — contains the new secret (shown once)

post.summary: Confirmation de réinitialisation de mot de passe
post.description: Valide le token reçu par email et met à jour le mot de passe.

204.description: Mot de passe mis à jour

400.description: Token invalide, expiré ou mots de passe non concordants

post.description: Creates a new user account with phone number, name, password, and optional email. A wallet is automatically created.

post.summary: Demande de réinitialisation de mot de passe
post.description: Envoie un lien de réinitialisation par email. Réponse identique qu'un compte existe ou non (anti-énumération).

200.description: Email envoyé si le compte existe

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's profile. Sensitive fields (phone, email, CNI) are masked.

patch.description: Partial update — only provided (non-null) fields are changed. fullName, email, and cniNumber are updatable here. Phone change requires OTP verification (separate endpoint). Password change requires current password (separate endpoint).

409.description: Email already used by another account

patch.description: Requires the current password for verification. New password must differ from the current one.

400.description: Passwords do not match or validation error

401.description: Authentication required or wrong current password

422.description: New password is the same as current

get.summary: Get a developer application by ID

404.description: Application not found or not owned by you

patch.description: Partial update — only provided fields are changed.

404.description: Application not found or not owned by you

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's wallet: available balance, frozen amount (in escrow), and total.

Returns a paginated, reverse-chronological list of wallet movements. Optionally filter by one or more movement types (comma-separated). Each entry includes before/after balance snapshots for full auditability.
Returns a single payout request. Must belong to the authenticated user.

404.description: Payout not found or access denied

get.description: Returns whether MFA is enabled for the authenticated user.
Generates a TOTP secret and returns a QR code (Base64 data URL) and backup codes. Step 1 of enrollment.

200.description: QR code and backup codes returned

get.description: Returns the full detail of a single transaction. User must be buyer or seller.

404.description: Transaction not found or access denied

get.description: Returns the full detail of a dispute. User must be initiator or respondent.

404.description: Dispute not found or access denied

delete.description: Permanently deactivates the key. This cannot be undone — create a new key if needed.

RegisterApplicationRequest.description: Request to register a new developer application on the Katika API platform

description.description: Short description of what your application does
description.example: E-commerce platform connecting buyers and sellers

websiteUrl.description: Public URL of your application or product

logoUrl.description: URL of your application logo (PNG or SVG, recommended 128x128)

organizationName.description: Legal or trading name of your organization

organizationSize.description: Number of employees in your organization

useCase.description: Detailed description of how you intend to use the Katika API
useCase.example: We use Katika escrow to protect both buyers and sellers in our marketplace, ensuring funds are only released when delivery is confirmed.

contactEmail.description: Technical contact email for API-related communications

termsAccepted.description: Must be true — indicates acceptance of Katika API Terms of Service

termsVersion.description: Version of the Terms of Service you are accepting

requestedScopes.description:
OAuth2 scopes your application requires. Allowed values:
- escrow.read    — Read escrow transactions
- escrow.write   — Create and update escrow transactions
- payout.execute — Execute Mobile Money payouts
- dispute.read   — Read disputes
- dispute.write  — Open disputes and submit evidence
- webhook.read   — Read webhook event logs
Defaults to [escrow.read] if not specified.

webhookUrl.description: HTTPS endpoint to receive real-time event notifications (optional)

initialKeyName.description: Label for the first API key that will be created automatically

initialKeyEnvironment.description: Environment for the initial API key: SANDBOX (testing) or PRODUCTION

ApiKeyResponse.description: API key details. The `secret` field is only present immediately after creation or rotation — store it securely.

id.description: Unique identifier of the API key

keyPrefix.description: Key prefix for display and identification (not secret)

active.description: Whether this key is currently active

lastUsedAt.description: Timestamp of the last request made with this key

expiresAt.description: Expiry timestamp — null means the key never expires

secret.description:
**Shown ONCE at creation or rotation only.**
This is the full API key to include in the `X-Api-Key` request header.
Katika does not store the raw key — if you lose it, rotate to get a new one.
Format: `ktk_{env}_{43-char-base64url}`

termsAcceptedAt.description: Timestamp when Terms of Service were accepted

status.description: Current application status: PENDING_REVIEW | ACTIVE | SUSPENDED | REVOKED

tier.description: Rate limiting tier: FREE | BASIC | PROFESSIONAL | ENTERPRISE

webhookSecretConfigured.description: Whether a webhook secret is configured

oauth2ClientId.description: OAuth2 client_id (only set when authStrategy = OAUTH2)

suspendedReason.description: Reason for suspension (only present if status = SUSPENDED)

initialApiKey.description: Initial API key — **only present in the registration response**

webhookSecret.description: Raw webhook secret to use for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. Shown once — store securely.

CreateApiKeyRequest.description: Request to create a new API key for a developer application

environment.description: Target environment: SANDBOX for testing, PRODUCTION for live traffic

UpdateApplicationRequest.description: Partial update for a developer application. Only provided fields are updated.

OAuth2 Client Credentials.description: OAuth2 Client Credentials flow for machine-to-machine authentication. Requires a registered developer application with `authStrategy = OAUTH2`.

BearerAuth.description: JWT Bearer token issued by the Katika Authorization Server. Obtain via `POST /oauth2/token` with your client credentials, or via the BFF login flow.

ApiKeyAuth.description:
**API Key authentication** for developer applications.

Format: `ktk_live_<43-char-base64url>` (production) or `ktk_test_<...>` (sandbox).

Obtain your key by registering a developer application at `POST /api/developer/applications`.
Include the key in every request as the `X-Api-Key` HTTP header.

**Best for:** backends that already have their own authentication system and
simply need to call Katika on behalf of their platform.
ApiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
